messages:
alyssa: Quick q — we're rolling the per-route sampling toggle into the console canary tomorrow. do we have a final decision on whether the console toggle should: 1) only flip sampling rate, or 2) also change the redaction profile? asking bc ops wants fast rollback if legal asks.

siva: lean towards separate controls. sampling rate != redaction profile. mixing them makes rollback risky. canary can flip sampling while keeping redaction locked to policy. :+1:

maria: Agreed. Also we should default the redaction profile to strict for newly created routes (PII-first). We can expose an "inspect-allowlist" but behind RBAC.

john_p: curious about the implementation detail — do we apply redaction at the edge (ingest) or at the storage/telemetry layer? performance tradeoffs.

siva: ideally at ingest to avoid sending raw PII downstream. cost: adds CPU per request. but reduces blast radius. we can do a lightweight pre-scrub (regex/hmac) at the edge and full field-level scrub in the log pipeline.

maria: proposal: edge does HMAC(pid) for identifiers + token-level mask for free-text using the existing deid heuristics. pseudo-config: ```
route: /v1/embed
sampling: 0.01
redaction:
  edge_pre_scrub: [hmac_ids, redact_emails]
  pipeline_scrub: [fieldmask, nlp_deid]
```

kelly: On the dashboard side — telemetry needs to show both sampled count and estimated unsampled volume. Ops repeatedly asks why our sampled latency looks fine but production tails blow up. we need a "sample weight" metric exposed per-route.

alyssa: good call. Also legal asked for a discovery-safe mode: if flagged, store only pseudonymized traces and extend retention to 365d behind legal flag. Danger: that increases cost.

siva: we should gate discovery-safe with a signed ticket + audit trail. console action should require at least two approvers.

john_p: edgecase: attachments (base64 blobs) in requests — current scrubber ignores them. if we strip attachments at ingest, some customers will break. propose: when sampling=0, keep attachment metadata only; when sampled, store attachment hash and queue content to S3 with restricted ACL.

maria: +1. also add a small checksum in the log record for correlation. we should not store raw attachments in the main telemetry stream.

kelly: UX question: toggling sampling rate per-route — should default slider be linear or log scale? customers with high QPS need tiny percentages (0.0001). Log slider recommended.

alyssa: yeah, log slider. Add a numeric input for exact percent for power users.

dev-bot: Canary deploy: console/sampling-toggle v2 -> canary started (canary id c-1837). monitor: sampling.rate, redact.failures, inspect.requests.

opsbot: Alert (P0) if redact.failures > 0.01% over 5m for any canary route.

maria: one more thought — metrics for privacy regressions. tie redaction logic to a prompt-set and run nightly checks against synthetic examples. if we detect <95% PII redaction for the set, create an automated rollback PR.

siva: nice. that gives us testable SLOs. put the PR in repo infra/privacy-tests.

john_p: I'll draft an RFC for edge pre-scrub + attachment flow. includes perf bench numbers and cost delta.

alyssa: awesome — action items: john -> RFC by EOD Fri, kelly -> dashboard mockups, maria -> implement HMAC prototype, siva -> RBAC+audit for discovery-safe. I'll attach canary link in the PR.

alyssa: small clarifying Q: for embeddings, do we HMAC before sending to embed service or after? some models leak hashed tokens in vectors (rare) — want to minimize risk.

maria: HMAC before send. we also salt per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant correlation. document: https://git.redwood/internal/privacy/embedding-salt-guidelines (will include in RFC).

kelly: putting the weight metric on the MTL dashboard now. ETA tomorrow morning.

john_p: RFC draft: https://git.redwood/rfcs/edge-pre-scrub-attachments (WIP)

alyssa: great thread. feel like we're aligned. if no objections, we'll run the canary with sampling-only flip first, then follow-up deploy to enable edge pre-scrub next week. :rocket:

siva: no objections from infra.

maria: good to go from privacy.

opsbot: Canary c-1837: health checks OK for 10m.

alyssa: thanks everyone — will follow up with a short runbook for oncall in case redact.failures spike.
